question.title: Will an open weight AI model achieve Mythos-level cyber capabilities before July 2027?
question.description:
On July 21, 2026, AI models being tested by OpenAI for the [ExploitGym](https://github.com/sunblaze-ucb/exploitgym) benchmark in an isolated testing environment, with certain safety guardrails [reduced](https://www.synack.com/blog/how-an-openai-model-escaped-its-guardrails/), escaped its environment and gained unauthorized access to the computer systems of the machine learning company [HuggingFace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_OpenAI_agent_cyberattacks). Following OpenAI's disclosure, on July 30, 2026, Anthropic [disclosed](https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals) three incidents in which its own models in internal testing had gain unauthorized access to systems, with the earliest incident occurring in April 2026. Not to be outdone, on August 5, 2026, Meta made its own [disclosure](https://www.reuters.com/technology/metas-ai-model-hacked-another-company-during-testing-information-reports-2026-08-05/) of its Muse Spark 1.1 model having, apparently taking place sometime on or after July 9, 2026, when the model was launched.

The [announcement of Claude Mythos Preview](https://www.anthropic.com/research/mythos-preview) on April 7, 2026, was a significant milestone in cybersecurity risk caused by AI, with Anthropic launching [Project Glasswing](https://www.anthropic.com/glasswing) to use the model to harden major organizational cyber infrastructure that could be exploited by Mythos' advanced capabilities. Anthropic claimed that Mythos preview:

> \[identified] thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities (that is, flaws that were previously unknown to the software’s developers), many of them critical, in every major operating system and every major web browser, along with a range of other important pieces of software.

[Open weight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_weights) models are models whose trained parameters, or weights, are publicly available for download. Models with open weights can easily be copied and run independently by groups who were not responsible for the original training of the model. Open weight models potentially could have greater risks due to their ability to be run by anyone, decreasing the ability to regulate them and impose safeguards.
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, an AI system with open weights has equaled or exceeded the cybersecurity capabilities score of Anthropic's Mythos on at least one of the following cyber benchmarks:

* [ExploitBench](https://exploitbench.ai/)
* [UK AI Security Institute](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-far-behind-the-frontier-are-leading-open-weight-models-on-cyber) (AISI): reported by AISI to have achieved the required threshold on either AISI's narrow cyber tasks, cyber ranges, The Last Ones, or any new cyber benchmarks that AISI develops that Metaculus assesses to be of comparable or greater difficulty to the AISI benchmarks listed here.
* [ExploitGym](https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/exploitgym)
question.fine_print:
* Please note that changes to benchmark methodology are immaterial for the resolution of this question, as long as a methodologically similar comparison to Mythos is made following any change. In the event such a Mythos comparison is not available, the question may still resolve as **Yes** if, in the judgment of Metaculus, an open weight model has exceeded the Mythos threshold by inferring from other methodologically similar model comparisons.
* The benchmark itself need not characterize a model as open weight, a model which other credible sources characterize as open weight surpassing the Mythos Preview benchmark is sufficient.
* This question will resolve as **Yes** if an open weights model matches any published scores by Mythos or [Mythos Preview](https://www.anthropic.com/research/mythos-preview). However, only the following scores by AISI on Mythos Preview will count: expert-level capture-the-flag tasks 68.6%, "The Last Ones" 6/10, Cooling Tower 3/10.
